Driving the next generation of wealth.

Digital assets are redefining how wealth is created, used, and transferred. Since 2018 at Nexo, we have been building the future model of financial wealth - dynamic, accessible, and designed for a new generation of forward-thinking investors.

But technology alone doesn’t drive progress. People do.

We are a team of builders, strategists, analysts, creatives, and operators united by a shared mindset: advancement. We move fast, think long term, and take ownership. We challenge ideas, not people. We value clarity over noise and impact over optics.

What makes Nexo different?

We shape industry trends. We rethink how wealth works and build solutions that reflect that belief.

That requires a certain kind of person.

You will thrive here when you think independently and act decisively, take ownership without waiting for permission, and care deeply about quality, long-term value, and disciplined execution. The people who succeed at Nexo bring analytical depth, sound judgment, and resilience - but also curiosity and the drive to keep improving.

This is an environment for people who want to lead, create, and elevate what already exists. If building what’s next excites you, you’ll feel at home at Nexo.

Official website: nexo.com

Your role:

  • Team Leadership: Lead, develop, and scale Nexo's local marketing team in Argentina. Set standards, run weekly cadences, and own performance management.
  • Local Growth Strategy: Define the marketing strategy for Argentina across brand awareness and acquisition. Translate Nexo's global priorities into market-specific plays that reflect local user behavior, regulation, and competitive dynamics.
  • Bridge with HQ: Act as the strategic interface between the AR team and central Paid, Partnerships, Creative, Web/SEO, Lifecycle, and Analytics teams. Make sure global initiatives land well locally and local insight flows back to HQ.
  • Market Intelligence & Channel Mapping: Maintain a live overview of Argentina's crypto and finance landscape - including publishers, influencer ecosystems, affiliates, events, and regional ad platforms.
  • HNWI Acquisition: Develop personas, targeting strategies, and localized messaging that resonate with Argentina's high-net-worth and mass-affluent investors. Identify premium channels and moments to engage them effectively.
  • Customer Experience Optimization: Audit key customer touchpoints (landing pages, onboarding flows, help center, FAQs) and collaborate with central teams to prioritize improvements and localization.
  • Data-Driven Insights: Translate findings into clear, actionable briefs and test hypotheses to improve funnel performance and growth efficiency.
  • Brand Voice: Adapt value propositions and messaging to Argentina, ensuring that all communications feel native and culturally relevant.
  • Brand Reputation & Risk Monitoring: Track brand mentions, community sentiment, and potential risks, proposing timely responses or mitigations.

Key Metrics (KPIs):

  • Funded accounts in Argentina, including HNWI share.
  • Customer LTV and LTV/CAC payback for AR cohorts.
  • Market penetration: Nexo funded accounts as a percentage of the active AR crypto investor base.

What makes you stand out:

  • 10-15+ years in senior marketing roles, with a demonstrated track record of leading marketing teams in Argentina or LATAM.
  • Direct people-management experience - you've hired, coached, and grown specialists, and you know how to set a standard without micromanaging.
  • Deep knowledge of the Argentine crypto, fintech, or wealth market - channels, partners, regulation, and culture.
  • Proven experience shaping positioning, messaging, and channel strategy in a fast-moving environment.
  • Hands-on crypto user with strong understanding of local crypto culture, media, and terminology.
  • Analytical mindset - skilled in turning complex data into actionable insights; experience with GA4, MMPs, and competitive intelligence tools.
  • Strong stakeholder management - able to align global HQ priorities with local market realities.
  • Bias for action, structured thinking, and high editorial standards.
  • Native Spanish; professional English.
  • Experience in fintech, crypto scale-ups, or financial services, with an existing network of relevant partners, publishers, and creators.

Nexo Benefits:

  • Competitive and rewarding remuneration package.
  • Hybrid work model: primarily office-based with scheduled home office flexibility.
  • Comprehensive additional health insurance as part of our wellness program.
  • Language class discounts to support continuous personal and professional growth.
  • A dynamic and inspiring environment with cutting-edge projects.
  • Career development opportunities in a global leader driving the next generation of wealth.

descriptions.job-0dxntq4:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career. 

About the team

Global Business Services’ (GBS) Commercial Solutions team ensures operational and programmatic excellence across deal cycles, increases revenue through the development of transformative commercial constructs, and drives closure of Stripe’s sold portfolio. The team's reach is widespread across Stripe, not exclusive to one sales segment or geographical region; GBS drives change across go-to-market, positively impacting Stripe users, and cross-functional teams. GBS’s priorities are set through the direction of Stripe leadership and executive vision, partnership with sales and cross-functional organizations, as well as User feedback and market insights. This role sits within Global Business Practices’ Commercial Solutions team, responsible for developing, launching, and maintaining commercial constructs and programs to drive revenue for Stripe.

What you’ll do

Stripe’s Global Business Services’ Commercial Solutions team is looking for a Commercial Lead to own the end-to-end programmatic development of commercial and GBS launch readiness programs that drive revenue for Stripe. Programs have a large scope and/or impact, including ownership of the development and support of first-of-their-kind commercialization efforts, ongoing program support (from pre-launch to post-launch), custom deal support related to the program, related enablement and communications, and acting as a change agent across the business.

You will be responsible for the end-to-end management of commercial and/or GBS launch readiness programs, driving cross-organizational alignment through the delivery of related outputs. This role requires a background in program management and commercial programs, change management experience, and a strong understanding of and experience in scaling global, cross-organizational mechanisms.

You will have experience in program ownership and management, custom pricing strategies, and supporting selling motions. You will have strong communication skills and executive presence to effectively communicate with Stripes, from sellers and Deal Strategies through to senior leadership. You will love this job if you are a natural relationship and mechanism builder.

Responsibilities

  • Independently lead large-scale, cross-functional commercial or GBS launch readiness programs that have Stripe-wide impact, often first-of-their-kind programs and initiatives.
  • Manage and lead highly complex programs that require considerable resources and high levels of functional and technical integration and knowledge.
  • Support the commercial program deal motion, partnering with Deal Pricing and/or Deal Strategy Strategists, sellers, and internal stakeholders to create custom commercial approaches.
  • Work cross-functionally with sales teams, sales leaders, services and support teams, product teams, and other cross-functional teams to develop, launch, and scale commercial programs, continuously evolving the ways Stripe goes to market to support commercialization efforts.
  • Identify, surface, and address systemic, broad issues and gaps, proposing holistic solutions to address root causes.
  • Work through complex programmatic problems at scale across go-to-market and Stripe, proposing creative solutions.
  • Partner with cross-functional teams such as Legal, Finance, Accounting, service teams, and product teams to resolve and remove internal blockers.
  • Act as a liaison among Sales, Deal Pricing and Deal Strategy Strategists, and other stakeholders for custom elements.
  • Run meetings, working sessions, and exercises that help the leadership team improve effectiveness among themselves and across the organization.
  • Advocate on behalf of a position and quickly gain cross-functional alignment on that position.
  • Quickly build credibility and trust with internal stakeholders.
  • Lead projects to solve existing commercialization issues.

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • BA/BS degree in Business, Technology, Finance, or Economics.
  • 10+ years of experience in program management, commercial strategy, economics, deal management, or pricing, including ownership of program strategy or business operations and direct experience in commercial pricing model program management, deal management, and/or oversight.
  • Experience driving cross-team mechanism development end to end, including ideation, planning, execution, launch, and post-launch support.
  • Experience working in ambiguous, quickly scaling environments, with a high degree of agency.
  • Experience engaging with senior executives on high-priority initiatives, as well as the ability to work effectively across internal and external organizations.
  • Ability to articulate and understand business strategy at the C-suite level to gain credibility and advise organizations on how best to achieve their business goals through commercial programs.
  • Strong written and verbal communication, presentation, negotiation, and project management skills.
  • Ability to establish credibility and maintain working relationships with internal stakeholders involved with commercial constructs, including Legal, Finance, and Accounting.
  • Experience presenting data and metrics to senior leadership.
  • Strong ability to advocate for a position, even in the face of pushback.

Preferred qualifications

  • Direct commercial construct launch oversight and experience
  • Payments industry experience
  • MBA degree in Business, Technology, Finance, or Economics
  • Possess PgMP or PMP certification

It all started with an idea at Block in 2013. Initially built to take the pain out of peer-to-peer payments, Cash App has gone from a simple product with a single purpose to a dynamic ecosystem, developing unique financial products, including Afterpay/Clearpay, to provide a better way to send, spend, invest, borrow and save to our 50+ million monthly active customers. We want to redefine the world’s relationship with money to make it more relatable, instantly available, and universally accessible.

Today, Cash App has thousands of employees working globally across office and remote locations, with a culture geared toward innovation, collaboration and impact. We’ve been a distributed team since day one, and many of our roles can be done remotely from the countries where Cash App operates. No matter the location, we tailor our experience to ensure our employees are creative, productive, and happy.

The Role

Cash App Investing is seeking a Compliance Officer to lead and mature the compliance program for its FINRA/SEC-regulated investing business. Reporting to the Head of Global Regulated Entities at Block, you will provide senior compliance leadership across broker-dealer obligations, product advisory, regulatory engagement, governance, and team execution. This role will partner closely with Cash App Investing leadership, Product, Engineering, Legal, Risk, Financial Crimes, Operations, and Internal Audit to support responsible growth and strong regulatory outcomes.

You Will

  • Lead the Cash App Investing compliance program, including policies, procedures, controls, monitoring, testing, reporting, and governance.
  • Maintain and enhance written supervisory procedures, supervisory controls, escalation routines, and compliance operating processes.
  • Advise Product, Engineering, Operations, Marketing, Legal, and business leaders on investing product development, customer communications, and regulated activities.
  • Oversee core broker-dealer compliance obligations, including communications review, complaints, regulatory filings, books and records, employee supervision, product reviews, and issue management.
  • Lead or support FINRA, SEC, state, and other regulatory exams, inquiries, responses, remediation plans, and regulator engagement.
  • Partner with Financial Crimes Compliance on AML, suspicious activity monitoring, investigations, fraud, identity theft, and related regulatory expectations.
  • Oversee compliance considerations for third-party and outsourced functions, including clearing broker and vendor relationships.
  • Develop clear reporting for senior leadership, governance forums, and the Board on risks, issues, exams, remediation, and program maturity.
  • Lead and develop a compliance team with clear ownership, sustainable coverage, and strong accountability.

You Have

  • 10+ years of compliance experience, including significant experience in broker-dealer, securities, fintech, financial services, or similarly regulated environments.
  • Deep knowledge of FINRA and SEC requirements applicable to retail broker-dealers and digital investing platforms.
  • Experience serving in a senior compliance, chief compliance officer, deputy CCO, or comparable compliance leadership role.
  • Experience managing regulatory exams, regulatory inquiries, remediation plans, and regulator communications.
  • Strong understanding of supervisory controls, written supervisory procedures, communications review, complaints, books and records, regulatory filings, and product compliance.
  • Experience advising product, engineering, operations, legal, and business teams on regulated financial products.
  • Strong judgment, communication skills, and ability to make risk-based decisions in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead, coach, and develop compliance professionals.

Even Better

  • FINRA principal registration, such as Series 24, or ability to obtain required registrations promptly.
  • Series 7, Series 14, Series 63/65/66, or other relevant securities registrations.

Founded in Silicon Valley in 2009 by Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz, Andreessen Horowitz (aka a16z) is a venture capital firm that backs bold entrepreneurs building the future through technology. We are stage agnostic. We invest in seed to venture to growth-stage technology companies, across AI, bio + healthcare, consumer, crypto, enterprise, fintech, games, and companies building toward American dynamism. a16z has $100B+ under management across multiple funds.

We’ve established a team that is defined by respect for the entrepreneur and the company-building process; we know what it’s like to be in the founder’s shoes. We’ve invested in companies like Anduril, Airbnb, Coinbase, Cursor, Databricks, Deel, Figma, GitHub, Roblox, SpaceX, and Stripe. Our team is at the forefront of new technology, helping founders and their companies impact and change the world.

The Role

We're hiring a Lead Engineer, Incident Response to lead and shape a16z's detection and response team. This is a hands-on role: you'll spend a significant portion of your time investigating incidents, writing and reviewing detections, building automation, and making the harder technical response decisions. You'll also manage and develop the engineers on the team.

You'll build and improve detection and response capabilities across the firm's cloud, SaaS, identity, and endpoint environments, shaping the roadmap, tooling, threat hunting, and response practices. You'll also develop capabilities to protect the firm against impersonation and fraud. You'll work closely with Security Engineering, IT, Legal, Compliance, and other cross-functional teams to put these capabilities into practice and turn lessons from incidents into better detections, tooling, and controls.

Venture capital firms face threats that extend beyond their infrastructure: capital call wire fraud, impersonation, and social engineering against employees and partners, alongside attacks by organized criminal and nation-state groups. Your work protects sensitive firm and limited partner (LP) information, financial transactions, and the relationships the firm depends on.

This role requires an in-office presence 2 days a week in our San Francisco, CA office.

To join our team, you should be excited to: 

  • Set the detection and response roadmap, prioritizing the threats that matter most to the firm and measuring detection coverage, alert quality, and response effectiveness
  • Lead and develop engineers through coaching, feedback, performance management, and technical reviews, working alongside them on investigations and engineering projects
  • Develop the team's ability to respond from triage through containment, eradication, and recovery, including vendor incidents. Lead major incidents, coordinate a16z's technical response with system owners and affected providers, and escalate decisions requiring leadership or Legal approval
  • Maintain and test response playbooks and escalation criteria through cross-functional tabletop exercises and incident simulations
  • Design and improve SIEM architecture and security logging with Security Engineering and IT, expanding detection coverage across cloud, identity, and endpoint environments, including EDR. Write, review, test, and tune detections as code, using relevant MITRE ATT&CK techniques to assess coverage and working with system owners to close visibility gaps
  • Run hypothesis-driven threat hunts informed by threat intelligence and prior investigations, turning findings into new detections
  • Build and improve brand protection capabilities including monitoring, investigation, and takedowns of lookalike domains, fraudulent websites, and social media accounts
  • Build AI-assisted response automation. Evaluate accuracy and reliability before deployment and define where human judgment and approvals are required
  • Keep technical and non-technical stakeholders aligned during incidents, including IT, Legal, Compliance, Finance, and investing teams. Clearly communicate impact, uncertainty, response options, and next steps
  • Develop the team's postmortem practices, lead reviews of root causes and contributing factors, and drive corrective actions to completion with the teams responsible for remediation
  • Participate in the Security team's on-call rotation

Minimum Qualifications

  • 9+ years of incident response or detection and response experience, or equivalent demonstrated impact, with depth in cloud incident response across AWS and GCP
  • Prior experience managing security engineers, including coaching and performance management, while remaining technically hands-on
  • A track record of building and leading detection and response programs, making architecture and prioritization decisions, and delivering measurable improvements
  • Experience leading high-stakes incidents across cloud, SaaS, identity, and endpoint environments, including forensic investigation, containment, recovery, and postmortems
  • Strong detection engineering skills, including SIEM query languages or rule formats such as KQL or Sigma, detection-as-code, testing, and tuning
  • Experience designing SIEM and security log pipelines and using cloud logs, endpoint detection and response (EDR), and security orchestration and automation (SOAR) tools in investigations and response. We value transferable capability over experience with a specific product
  • Experience running hypothesis-driven threat hunts and investigating sophisticated attacks, including identity compromise, social engineering, and data exfiltration
  • Strong Python skills and experience building and reviewing maintainable security automation
  • Working knowledge of AI and agent systems, including their limitations and security risks when used in triage and response workflows
  • Experience leading cross-functional security work and communicating incident impact, uncertainty, and technical trade-offs clearly to non-technical stakeholders and senior leaders
  • Sound judgment under pressure, balancing security risk and business impact and recognizing when to escalate
  • Low ego, high empathy, and a track record of effective collaboration across teams

GCIH or an equivalent incident response certification is a bonus but not required.

The anticipated salary range for this role is between $295,000 - $347,000, actual starting pay may vary based on a range of factors which can include experience, skills, and scope.

This role is eligible to participate in the a16z carry program and various discretionary bonus programs as well as benefit and perquisite plans including health, dental, vision, disability, life insurance, 401K plan, vacation, and sick leave.

  • We take a long view of relationships, because we are in the relationship business 
  • We believe in the future and bet the firm that way
  • We are all different, we recognize that, and we win
  • We celebrate the good times
  • We do it for the team
  • We play to win

We hire candidates of any race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital or family status, disability, Veteran status, and any other status. descriptions.job-07t74xo:
Role Overview

The Customer Success Manager is a hands-on player-coach who owns the external link with our Ethena Pay users. You'll be the single accountable owner of the customer experience after signup. On day one you'll be in the queue answering tickets yourself, including the hard ones. For the 1st 6 months, expect roughly 70% doing the work and 30% building the operations of the function. You’ll be the 1st, so there is huge potential career growth baked in here. You’ll find your maximum ability and seniority level within the team, as the need for a larger support and payments ops org grows around you.

Support is a key place a money product can truly stand out, and few competitors set a high bar We want users to tell other people how good our support is, and we want ticket volume to fall because the reasons for them are being removed. You'll sit directly inside the product team, working closely with Engineering, Finance, Compliance, and our GTM team.

Role Responsibilities

  • Own the queue personally: handle most inbound tickets yourself early on, own Zendesk end to end (triage, tagging, macros, help centre). You’ll publish, and hold yourself to, the first response and resolution targets.

  • Set a support quality bar users talk about: define what best-in-class looks like in writing, measure satisfaction and public sentiment properly, run response QA, and contact affected users before they contact us.

  • Turn support into measured input for product and engineering: a standing weekly read by cluster and contact rate, every defect routed with impact and an owner, and clear escalation thresholds so emergencies move fast and routine volume never interrupts engineering.

  • Automate the work: remove the causes of the largest clusters through product fixes, self-serve answers and automated status updates, use AI-assisted triage with a human check wherever money is involved, and track falling effort per user as an explicit goal.

  • Be the named operational owner of our rails vendors (card issuer, on/off-ramp, KYC and wallet partners), with escalation paths, a vendor incident log and evidence for commercial reviews.

  • Bring the manual money workflows under documented control: runbooks, four-eyes checks and audit trails for reconciliation, disputes and chargebacks, refunds, stuck withdrawals, fraud triage and KYC edge cases, working with parent Finance and Compliance.

  • Build and lead the operations function: bring support across the ticket queue, Telegram and X into one operation, own user-facing incident comms, run an operations KPI dashboard, and grow a small front line and payments-ops team toward follow-the-sun and multilingual coverage.

Required Skills and Experience

  • Previously run support or operations for a live consumer money product where mistakes moved, lost or delayed real customer funds, such as a neobank, payments company, card program, exchange or crypto money app.

  • Owned operational KPIs and reported them regularly to executive and product audiences, with examples of numbers you moved and how you moved them.

  • A track record of reducing the work, not just absorbing it: contact rates brought down or clusters engineered out, with before-and-after numbers.

  • A support experience you built that users praised, backed by satisfaction or sentiment data.

  • Handled money-movement exceptions end to end, such as disputes and chargebacks, refunds, failed or stuck withdrawals, reconciliation breaks, or KYC and sanctions escalations. You've also managed third-party vendors operationally, including getting a live production problem fixed.

  • A player-coach who has done the work and built a small team or contracted capacity around it, including outsourced support and coverage across time zones or languages.

  • Agent-native working: you use AI tools to cluster tickets, draft macros and help-centre content, and build reports, and you check the output for accuracy and tone.
descriptions.job-019br7g:
Why this role exists

Our web experience is a company asset, owned and managed by marketing. It is a strategic growth platform and our most effective engine for brand, demand, customer engagement and education, and revenue.

We are hiring a Web Strategy and Execution Lead to run it that way. This is not a website management role. It is an ownership role for a commercial platform, accountable for what the asset returns to the business.

You will set the strategy for how our web estate earns attention, converts intent, educates customers, and contributes pipeline and revenue. You will then build, test, and ship against that strategy on a permanent cycle.

Primary accountability

Increase the commercial contribution of our web estate through strategy, customer experience, conversion optimization, content, search, technology, and continuous experimentation.

What you will own

Web strategy and development

  • Own the strategy and roadmap for our web estate, tied directly to commercial outcomes rather than page count or release volume.
  • Define what the platform is for by audience and stage, from first exposure through evaluation, purchase, onboarding, and ongoing customer engagement.
  • Make the case for investment with a clear view of cost, return, and opportunity cost. Prioritize ruthlessly and be willing to retire what does not perform.
  • Build the operating rhythm: intake, prioritization, delivery, measurement, and iteration.

Conversion and growth

  • Own conversion performance end to end, from traffic quality through to qualified pipeline and revenue contribution.
  • Run a continuous experimentation program with a live hypothesis backlog, clear success criteria, and honest read-outs on what did not work.
  • Optimize the full journey rather than isolated pages: entry points, navigation, forms, demo and trial flows, self-serve routes, and handoffs to sales and e-commerce.
  • Partner with demand generation on campaign landing experiences, personalization, and lead quality.

Content and search

  • Own the search strategy across search engine optimization (SEO), answer engine optimization (AEO), and generative engine optimization (GEO), so we are found and cited in traditional search and in AI-generated answers.
  • Build the technical, structural, and content foundations that support discoverability at scale: information architecture, schema, site performance, internal linking, and content governance.
  • Work with brand, product marketing, and content to turn our domain expertise into web content that ranks, converts, and holds up to scrutiny from a compliance audience.
  • Track share of visibility against the categories we intend to lead.

User experience and customer experience

  • Be the advocate for the user inside the business. Know the journeys, the friction, and the drop-off points, and be able to evidence all three.
  • Run continuous research and feedback loops: session analysis, user testing, surveys, and direct customer input.
  • Raise the quality bar on usability, accessibility, and performance across every device and market we serve.
  • Extend the experience beyond acquisition into onboarding, education, and existing-customer engagement.

Technology and execution

  • Own the web technology stack and the roadmap for it, including content management, testing and personalization tooling, analytics, and the integrations that connect web to our marketing and revenue systems.
  • Make build, buy, and partner decisions with a clear view of speed, cost, and long-term maintainability.
  • Manage agency and contractor relationships where we use them, and hold them to the same standards we hold ourselves to.
  • Work with information technology (IT), security, and data teams on privacy, consent, resilience, and compliance requirements.

Data and measurement

  • Define the measurement framework for the asset: the metrics that matter, how they connect to pipeline and revenue, and how we report them.
  • Build the instrumentation and attribution needed to make that framework trustworthy, in partnership with marketing operations and data.
  • Turn analysis into decisions. Every significant change should have a hypothesis behind it and a read-out after it.
  • Give the wider business a clear, regular view of how the platform is performing commercially.

Who you will work with

This is a senior role with management and strategic responsibility for the success of Luno's global OTC desks, reporting to the Head of Treasury. You'll manage OTC principal traders across several markets, ensuring that they act within defined limits at all times and you’ll ensure that flow from institutions, corporates and professional traders is profitably traded on a risk-adjusted basis. Sitting within our Treasury team, you'll work with the heads of our Stablecoin and Payment / Remittances initiatives, in-country teams and relationship managers to turn that flow into a consistently profitable book.

Your mission will be: 

Team management

  • Manage and mentor a team of traders, fostering a culture of high performance, risk awareness, and commercial proactivity.

Manage P/L and risk

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About Production Engineering

Production Engineering is Ramp's infrastructure ownership layer. We exist to make Ramp faster, more reliable, and more scalable — and we do that by being embedded in the problems, not adjacent to them.

A few things that define how we operate:

  • One team, one company, one objective. There is no "infra team" and "product team" — there is Ramp. We share the company's goals as our own. When a product team struggles with reliability or scalability, that is our struggle.

  • If reliability or scalability is at risk, we own it. We don't wait to be invited, and we don't ask whose code it is. If a system is slow, if it breaks, if it won't scale — that's ours to lead, regardless of where it lives in the stack.

  • We go first, and we go fast. When the path isn't obvious, we don't wait for someone else to find it. We move with urgency, propose the solution, align the stakeholders, and stay in until it's done — not until our ticket is closed.

  • We lead the way. We find the next problem before it finds us. And when we solve it, we don't just fix it for ourselves — the patterns and standards we establish become the foundation the rest of Ramp builds on. That's not a side effect of the job; it's the job.

  • We stay calibrated. Speed means nothing if we're moving in the wrong direction. We regularly stop and ask honestly whether what we're working on is still the highest-leverage thing we could be doing — the discipline that makes sure our effort compounds toward what actually matters.

You cannot build the future of finance on shaky infrastructure.

Our Teams

Production Engineering is organized into teams — but we think about teams differently. Teams are mutable. We build them around what needs to be done, not around what we need to do given the teams we already have. The structure below reflects our current priorities; it will evolve as Ramp does.

Right now, we operate across four areas:

  • Compute — the foundation everything runs on: container orchestration, networking, load balancing, edge infrastructure, and the deployment systems that get code from engineers' laptops to production reliably and at scale

  • Storage — databases, caching, object storage, and the data infrastructure that underpins everything

  • Workflows & Messaging — the systems that power Ramp's financial workflows and event-driven architecture

  • Developer Infrastructure — the platform that makes every builder at Ramp faster and more autonomous: observability, cost attribution, and CI/CD systems that give teams visibility into what they build and what it costs

What You'll Do

Production Engineers at Ramp are full software engineers who happen to specialize in infrastructure. You write production code, you own systems end-to-end, and you drive technical outcomes across the organization — not just within your team.

As a Tech Lead & Manager, you are a hands-on player-coach: you will lead and grow a team while remaining directly engaged in the technical work. Management at Ramp does not mean stepping away from the technology or the code. You will help set direction, develop engineers, and work alongside the team to deliver consequential infrastructure outcomes.

Day to day, you will:

  • Build, coach, and grow a high-performing team. Create clarity, give direct feedback, mentor engineers, and help each person expand their technical judgment, ownership, and leadership.

  • Set technical direction for your team’s domain. Identify the highest-leverage problems, define a path forward, bring the right people along, and stay engaged with the team until the work is delivered.

  • Build and operate critical infrastructure across Ramp's compute, storage, messaging, and observability stack — owning the systems that handle real financial transactions at scale.

  • Drive architectural change — not just flag problems. When you surface a reliability or scalability issue, you own the path forward: you propose the solution, find the owners across engineering, and stay in until it's resolved.

  • Partner with product teams at the design phase — reviewing architectures, embedding golden paths, and making it easy to build correctly the first time.

  • Build Ramp's next level of scale — you'll be a hands-on contributor to the most consequential infrastructure shift happening right now: our move to a cellular architecture, enabling Ramp to scale, reach international markets, operate in highly regulated and constrained environments (e.g. FedRAMP), and deliver on enterprise-grade SLAs.

  • Enable AI-native engineering — as Ramp builds increasingly AI-powered products, PE is the team that makes sure the platform can support them. You'll proactively partner with product teams on AI infrastructure patterns, define the golden paths that turn one-off solutions into reusable foundations, and stay ahead of emerging challenges before they become blockers.

  • Build developer tooling and self-service infrastructure — so that other teams can answer their own questions (cost, performance, reliability) without involving PE.

  • Participate in on-call rotation — and more importantly, use every incident as a signal to eliminate the root cause, not just resolve the symptom.

  • Lead across the company — PE doesn't just review designs or show up when called. We proactively initiate cross-team architectural reviews, and we take full ownership of company-wide reliability and scalability initiatives: identifying the problem, proposing the solution, aligning the stakeholders, and staying in until it's done.

What We Look For

We don't hire for a checklist. We hire for the instincts that make someone exceptional on this team.

The mindset we're looking for:

  • You love building teams, mentoring engineers, and helping people grow—and you are equally energized by writing code, reviewing designs, and digging into complex distributed systems.

  • You are a true player-coach. You know when to coach, delegate, and create space for others to lead; you also know when your direct technical involvement will create the most leverage.

  • You can set a technical direction, bring people along, and then lock in with the team to make it happen.

  • You do not believe managing engineers means stepping away from the technology or the code.

  • You can't walk past something broken without wanting to fix it — and you don't stop at the workaround. You find the root cause and eliminate the class of problem.

  • You think in systems, not tasks. You understand that "fixing the bug" is step one; making it so the bug can't happen again is the job.

  • You move with urgency but without chaos. You know when to go fast and when to slow down and do it right.

  • You treat product teams as your users. You build for them, communicate with them proactively, and measure success by how much faster they can ship. But you're also an owner — when something is broken or blocking, you don't wait to be asked. We win when our customers win.

  • You leave things better than you found them. Every system you touch, every process you encounter — you move it forward. Not always dramatically, but always directionally. You picked it up in a certain state; you leave it in a better one.

  • You are equally comfortable reading a database query plan, reviewing a system design doc, writing a Terraform module, and jumping into an incident at 2am.

BitGo is looking for a design leader who still designs. You will manage and mentor the design team, own the design system, and sit next to the Chief Product Officer on business strategy.

This is a player-coach role, and we mean it literally. You will carry your own design surfaces and ship them, alongside leading the team. Expect roughly 50% hands-on IC work to start, decreasing as the team scales. It will not go to zero — the person setting the craft bar should be practicing at it.

We are not a design-forward company today. We intend to become one, and we want you to lead that shift.

The team you will lead

The design team is small, senior, and self-sufficient. Each designer owns a wide vertical outright — trading, staking, DeFi vaults, earn, wallets, financing — with deep product context and strong opinions about the work. They are running at capacity, which is part of why this role carries real IC load: you will pick up the retail mobile experience and design system rather than distributing that work across a team that is already full.

What they have asked for is specific, and we are hiring against it: a leader who gets into the work early with product and engineering rather than arriving at the end, who can critique craft because they still practice it, who tells them plainly what the next level requires, and who gives the team air cover so they can do the deep work instead of patching to hit dates.

What you will own

  • Your own design work. You will own surfaces directly and ship them at the quality bar you are asking of everyone else. Discovery through spec, in Figma, in the reviews, on the hard problems.
  • The team's growth. Invest in each designer individually. Be explicit about what the next level requires and give people the work that gets them there. Feedback should be candid, specific, and about the craft. Respect the ownership designers already have — autonomy is how this team works best, and your job is to raise the ceiling, not take the pen.
  • Design's standing in the company. Amplify the team's visibility, voice, and strategic impact. Represent design in strategy, roadmap, and architecture conversations, and push for the client experience when nobody else in the room will.
  • Upstream involvement. Join product and engineering at discovery, not at handoff. Shape long-term roadmaps with PMs so the team builds toward a direction instead of absorbing late changes.
  • The design system. Own the system and component library end to end: tokens, patterns, governance, contribution model, and adoption across product teams. Translate company strategy into a system flexible enough that teams ship scalable experiences rather than one-off patches.
  • Systems design. Our platform spans seven product areas with shared primitives — accounts, wallets, assets, entitlements, approvals. Design the system, not the screen.
  • The discipline. Establish UX and systems thinking as a practice the whole organization runs on, not a stage a design team owns. Product managers, engineers, and business leads should be able to frame a client problem, map the system it lives in, and evaluate a solution against real client needs. That is how we ship value to every client type we serve, in every market we operate in — rather than a set of features that work for the loudest account.
  • How we work. Establish the processes a small team needs to move fast without losing quality: critique, documentation, design review, and clean handoffs with engineering. Set the quality bar and hold it, including for AI-assisted work.
  • Technical depth. Read a technical design, understand the constraint, and decide with engineering where to compromise, where to hold, and where a broader change is worth the cost. Get into the mechanics with the team on the hard edge cases — the crypto ones and the design ones.
  • The face of design. Be present and known internally, and represent BitGo design externally with clients, partners, and candidates.

What success looks like

By six months: the design system has a clear owner, a versioned component library, and measurable adoption. Product teams stop reinventing patterns. You have shipped design work of your own that the team points to as the standard. Every designer knows what their next level requires and has work that supports getting there.

By 12 months: design is in the room early on strategy, not late on execution. Product and engineering partners frame problems in client terms without being asked. The team has grown in size and capability. At least one flagship surface has shipped with a coherent, systemized experience clients notice.

Who you are

  • Experience leading design in financial services. Digital assets, or another domain of genuinely complex technical flows, strongly preferred.
  • You have built and owned a design system at scale, not just used one.
  • Hands-on in Figma and a role model for craft. You are shipping design work today, not describing work you shipped four years ago. You can sit in a critique and give feedback that is specific enough to act on.
  • Deep in UX. Strong product thinking, logical reasoning, and decisions grounded in data rather than taste alone.
  • You have managed designers and made them better. You care about how the team is doing, not only what it ships.
  • Technically literate. Comfortable with APIs, data models, and engineering trade-offs.
  • Direct communicator. You can hold a position with a Chief Product Officer, an engineering lead, or a client, and change your mind when the argument is better.
  • You want the mandate. Turning a technical, compliance-heavy platform into a design-led one is the appeal, not the obstacle.

Helpful, not required

Every person and every business connected to the Global Financial Internet. Built on Mural.

That's the world Mural is building. This role is one of the hands on the brush.

About Mural

Mural is regulated financial infrastructure across the US and Latin America. The whole stack, one partner. Companies build cross-border financial products on us using our API. We carry the licenses, the compliance, and the failure states, so they go live in weeks instead of months. Under the hood, fiat and blockchain run as one system. Their customers never see any of it. Money comes in, money goes out, and it just gets there.

We've processed over $2 billion across US dollar, stablecoin, and international rails. That includes USDC and USDT on major blockchains, ACH and wire in the US, and local rails across Latin America and Europe (PIX, SPEI, Bre-B, CBU/CVU, SEPA). Customers include Deel, Bolt, Opera, Koywe, Taxdome, Uniswap, Movii, and more. We've successfully raised our Series A. And we're an AI-native company. Agentic tools are how we build, operate, and scale.

The Role

As companies expand globally, holding, moving, and reconciling money becomes slow, fragmented, and fragile. And now, at an inflection point for global finance, stablecoins are emerging as the rails that fix that, but most companies don't yet know how to adopt them. That's where you come in.

You'll be one of our first sales hires, which means you're not just executing a playbook, you're helping write it. You'll work directly with our founders and leadership team to build pipeline, run deals, and close the customers that define our next chapter.

This role is about three things.

1. Full-Cycle Ownership

You own the entire deal from first touch to close. You'll source your own top-of-funnel through outbound prospecting, network activation, conference presence, and creative hustle, then carry that deal through discovery, technical evaluation, legal, and signature. No handing off to another team mid-cycle. You're accountable for the outcome.

2. Consultative, Technical Selling

We're not selling a simple SaaS subscription. We're selling infrastructure, and in a market where every company is trying to figure out what stablecoins mean for their business, there's a genuine opportunity to be a trusted advisor, not just a vendor. You'll need to go deep. Understand our API, understand how money moves globally, and help prospects connect the dots between where they are and where Mural can take them. The best reps here will be the ones who can speak the language of a CTO, a CFO, and a treasury team, sometimes in the same meeting.

3. Pipeline Generation & Revenue Growth

You'll carry an ambitious quota and be expected to hit it. You'll coordinate with marketing on inbound leads while building your own outbound engine in parallel. You'll track your pipeline rigorously, iterate on your approach constantly, and be ruthless about prioritizing the deals most likely to close and expand. We optimize for real revenue, not activity metrics.

Who You Are

You're a hunter and a closer. You know how to open doors and you know how to walk through them. You're not waiting for leads to land in your inbox. You're building relationships at conferences, sending thoughtful outbound, and finding the angle that gets a busy CFO to take a meeting.

You're technical enough to go deep. You don't need to be an engineer, but you need to love understanding how things work. You'll get into the weeds of our API, understand payment flows and treasury operations, and be able to explain complex infrastructure in plain language. Bonus points if you've sold developer tools, payments, or financial infrastructure before.

You're built for startups. You've worked in an early-stage environment before and you know what that means. No perfect process, limited resources, high ambiguity, and outsized impact. You don't need a large team behind you to execute. You move fast, make decisions, and figure things out.

You're a genuine advisor on stablecoins and global payments. The market is at an inflection point. Companies across every industry are trying to figure out how to adopt stablecoins, and most of them don't have a clear path. You see that as an opportunity, not a headwind. You stay sharp on the regulatory landscape, the technology, and the competitive dynamics, and you show up to every conversation as a genuine expert.

You're autonomous and obsessive about the details. You'll have direct access to our leadership team and real influence over how we go to market, but you won't need someone managing your schedule or your pipeline. You keep things organized, follow through on every commitment, and never let a deal die because of a dropped ball on your end.

What Success Looks Like

  • You're consistently hitting and exceeding quota through a combination of outbound discipline and sharp deal execution

  • Your pipeline is real. Qualified, progressing, and built on genuine relationships rather than inflated forecasts

  • You've become a trusted voice in the stablecoin and global payments space, known by the people building in this world

  • You've helped shape our sales playbook in ways that scale beyond you as we grow the team. The process, the pitch, and the objection handling

How We Work

We run on three principles.

2% better, every day. One percent for yourself, one percent for the people around you.

Telos. From the Greek word telos, meaning not just done but fulfilled. Everyone here is focused on one mission and knows each other's Telos.

Abundance. We can create anything we set our minds to, for ourselves, our partners, and our entire Mural family.

We're builders all the way down. Code is a medium, like paint. We choose honesty over polish and never claim what isn't true. We obsess over boring details, because trust is built in RFIs, refunds, and response times. And we hire for curiosity. It's a bar, not a poster.

Compensation & Benefits

  • Competitive base plus commission, with a quota that will push you and comp that reflects it

  • Meaningful early-stage equity

  • Health insurance

  • 401(k)

  • Visa sponsorship available

Location

New York City and LATAM. Relocation supported. Open to traveling to meet customers.

We named this company Mural because murals have always told the story of a community. They are made by hand, made together, painted onto the foundations of a place, and meant to outlast the people who started them. Every person who joins brings a new piece.

Now let's build a force of nature business, together.
